title: At four alpine sites, cross-species seedling clustering was clear at emergence but uncertain at season end
abstract: We tested whether supplied lower-elevation plant species recruited in the same subplots at four alpine sites in 2021. We used 10,900 supplied seeds, 160 physical subplots and 420 species units. An exact test retained each species incidence within site, warming, vegetation and strategy groups. The primary final live presence test gave 51 co-occurring species pairs versus 46 expected, with a null 95% range of 40-52 and two-sided p = 0.147. Recorded emergence gave 86 pairs versus 75.8 expected, range 69-83 and p = 0.00549. Emergence ratios stayed above one after each site or species omission, but statistical support was not universal. The emergence ratio was 1.48 in intact vegetation and 1.04 in gaps; this exploratory contrast does not identify a treatment interaction. A survival reference that also fixed final species incidence expected 49.83 pairs, consistent with the observed 51. The result distinguishes shared emergence sites from prior within-species clustering. It does not show a persistent common recruitment limit or explain a share of weak thermal tracking. One season, four sites, selected species and shared detection limit inference. Code, aggregate results, exact null distributions, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Observed cross-species pair counts and exact independent placement references. Species incidence totals, sites and treatments are held fixed.
